newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Davids says to end PFD merger talks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Davids says to end PFD merger talks.

text.p: Grocery wholesaler and retailer Davids Ltd said on Wednesday it would cease talks with PFD Food Services about a merger with its John Lewis Foodservice unit as part of a major rationalisation of its business and management.
The merger, which involved no cash outlay, would have created Australia's largest food service company.

The decision not to proceed is part of a rationalisation of Davids which includes an abnormal write-down of A$262.4 million. The company also said executive chairman and chief executive John David had resigned and would be replaced by Don Bourke.
"...Davids believes it is appropriate to cease discussions with PFD for a merger with John Lewis Foodservice at this time," the company said.
The merger had been scheduled to take effect from July 1.
Davids would have owned 60 percent and PFD 40 percent of the joint venture. John Lewis Food Service has annual sales of about A$400 million and PFD has sales of A$180 million.
Davids shares were down one cent at A$1.10 at 0315 GMT (1.15 p.m.). The stock has traded between A$1.10 and A$1.82 this year.
